qa.q: Do you work or are you a student?
qa.a: Well, actually, I suppose I'm both right now because I work as a teacher and I work on this podcast, and I also work on a separate course as well. But I'm also doing an online course at Aberdeen University. So, both, actually.

qa.q: Why did you choose this kind of work and studies?
qa.a: Well, if we talk about work, for example, then I picked it because, uh, first of all, I was interested in it, and then I stuck with it because I'm good at it. Uh, I always wanted to be a teacher. I like helping people achieve their goals. Um, I chose mathematics to study, well, actually, mathematics chose me, because I don't have, or I didn't have a qualification in this, so I study it now in order to make up for the deficit in what I know right now.

qa.q: Do you like this job and your studies?
qa.a: Oh, I love my job. It's wonderful. Um, I look forward to doing it more often in the future when all my courses are over. Um, as for the course itself, um, I suppose I like the idea of learning something new, but as for the subject of mathematics, I'm not exactly in love with it. I think I'd much rather do more things with English.

qa.q: What's the most interesting part in your work?
qa.a: Um, well, it's never boring. For example, like every day I work with people for different purposes, and I work with different age ranges, and of course, we work on a variety of subjects as well. Um, I guess my only regret is not doing it sooner, to be honest with you.

qa.q: What's the most difficult part in your work and studies?
qa.a: Uh, well, if we talk about my job, then I suppose, uh, the most frustrating aspect is that people are sometimes quite disorganized. I don't mean the students, they're allowed to be disorganized because they're all young people. But, um, sometimes the adults I have to work with can be quite disorganized, or they haven't had their expectations managed well, so they get quite disappointed. Um, it's not a disaster, it just makes things more difficult. Um, if we talk about, um, what I study, then I think the most difficult thing is the subject matter itself, because mathematics is difficult for me. I understand for some people it's easy, but for me, it's really not. I don't have a head for it. So that makes life a lot more complicated.

qa.q: What do you dislike about your work or studies?
qa.a: Um, well, I dislike that I have to deal with so many disorganized people, although it's not that many, it's maybe only a few, but it can still get a bit annoying. Um, and if we talk about mathematics, um, I don't like that it's such a struggle for me to get my head around different mathematical formula without a serious effort. Uh, for example, uh, linear equations or adding positive or negative numbers isn't my thing right now. It just means I have to put more effort in, but it can be quite difficult and, um, I don't like it when I put in the effort and I don't see the progress.

qa.q: What was your dream job when you were a child?
qa.a: Well, like I said before, I wanted to be a teacher. Um, I've always thought that's a great profession to have, and so far, I've not been proven wrong by this at all. I think it's been great.

qa.q: Have you changed your mind since then?
qa.a: Only in terms of the subject, because, well, I always wanted to be a teacher, then I narrowed my focus to English language teaching. Um, but it seems like I'm going to have to broaden my focus again because I want to be a primary school teacher, so you have to teach English, mathematics, uh, all of the other subjects related to this.

qa.q: What kind of work would you like to do in the future?
qa.a: Um, well, anything connected to education, I suppose. Um, unless it's anything to do with management or teacher training. I'm never doing that ever again once I'm finished with this.
